value: maize seed germination was 93.5% after sound treatment against 84.0% in untreated seeds
method: seeds imbibed 8 h, then 10 h of white noise at a constant 80 dB in a sound-proof chamber; control plates held in silence under the same conditions in the same chamber; germination tests were 10 replicates of 20 seeds each, one treated plate and one control plate per replicate (200 seeds per condition)
conditions: one cultivar (Duero), seeds six years old and stored at 4 C, low humidity, dark; germination scored over days; Results report only the 300 Hz tone among single frequencies as significantly higher than control, and removing the pericarp removed the sound effect

source.title: The effect of frequency-specific sound signals on the germination of maize seeds

quote: However, the percentage of germinated seeds was significantly higher after sound treatment (93.5% ± 1.0) than the observed in untreated seeds (84.0% ± 1.2).
note: Endpoint is seed germination after airborne sound, a physiological endpoint, so no receptor or sensory modality is established; the paper reports that removing the pericarp removed the effect, so a seed-coat route is possible. The sentence's treatment is the white noise (80 dB, 10 h) named in the preceding Results sentence; the 300 Hz tone and the 5000 and 12000 Hz tones are separate tests not logged here. Names: POWO page for Zea mays L. says accepted; WFO snapshot page lists Zea mays accepted. Licence: page prints 'This article is distributed under the terms of the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License'. value: blue light at night (16W + 8B) increased pepper internode length relative to the 16 h white light plus dark night control, to a lesser extent than blue plus far-red (16W + 8BFR) or far-red (16W + 8FR) at night
method: greenhouse pepper under 16 h white daytime light (6:00 to 22:00) followed by an 8 h night treatment (22:00 to 6:00): control 16W (darkness at night), continuous white light (24W), blue at night (16W + 8B), blue plus far-red at night (16W + 8BFR), far-red at night (16W + 8FR, Experiment 2); internode length measured at two harvests
conditions: Experiment 2: cultivars Maureno, Gina and Eurix, 40 plants per cultivar per treatment, destructive measurements on 10 plants per cultivar at 37 to 39 days in treatment and 6 per cultivar at 64 to 66 days; Experiment 1 used Maureno only with 72 plants per treatment; night-light intensities are in the paper's Table 1 and were not read; the abstract sentence logged does not say which cultivar or harvest, and the magnitude of internode increases differs by cultivar and date in the Results (not logged); Tukey-Kramer adjusted comparisons at 0.05, individual p values not printed

source.authors: Lanoue J, Little C, Hao X
source.title: The Power of Far-Red Light at Night: Photomorphogenic, Physiological, and Yield Response in Pepper During Dynamic 24 Hour Lighting

quote: The 16W + 8B treatment also increased internode length but to a lesser extent than 16W + 8BFR and 16W + 8FR.
note: Night-time light quality comparison against a dark-night control; the paper reads these as photomorphogenic responses, but this record logs only the internode endpoint and no photoreceptor is identified. Same abstract: 16W + 8B and 16W + 8BFR drove photosynthesis at night and gave a yield similar to 16W; continuous white light (24W) significantly reduced fruit production and Fv/Fm. Results note that in 'Eurix' 16W + 8FR produced taller plants than 16W + 8BFR. Names: POWO page for Capsicum annuum L. lists it under 'Accepted in' (no separate status line on the page); WFO snapshot page list.worldfloraonline.org/wfo-0001019982 gives accepted name.
